categories.title: Physical Twins · Identified Parameters
categories.delivers: a 3D representation coupled to a known physics model, with parameters fitted to the object's own observed motion
categories.description: Reconstruct an object or scene, couple it to a known physics model (MPM, spring–mass, rigid body, FEM, rods) and fit the physical parameters until simulated motion matches the observed motion. The result simulates *this* object under new forces.
categories.tagline: parameters fitted to its own motion

categories.title: Physical Twins · Assigned Parameters
categories.delivers: the same kind of physical twin, with parameters taken from a generative prior, a language model or a person rather than fitted to observed motion
categories.description: Couple a physics model to a reconstructed or generated 3D scene, but take the parameters from somewhere other than the object's own motion: a video-generation prior, a vision-language model, or a hand-set value. Mostly used for interactive 3D/4D content.
categories.tagline: parameters from priors or by hand

categories.title: Simulation-Ready Assets
categories.delivers: a single object in a standard simulator format (URDF, MJCF, USD, SDF) with joints, limits, collision shapes and inertia
categories.description: Turn scans, images or interaction videos of a real object into an asset any physics engine can load: parts, joints, limits, collision geometry and inertia, most often for articulated objects.
categories.tagline: one object in URDF / MJCF / USD

categories.title: Scene-Level Simulations & Digital Twins
categories.delivers: a whole environment (objects, layout, often a robot and a renderer) that runs inside a simulator
categories.description: Rebuild an entire real environment — a tabletop, a room, a street — inside a simulator, often with Gaussian splatting for realistic sensors, so that robots or vehicles can be trained and evaluated in it.
categories.tagline: a whole environment in a simulator

categories.title: Executable Simulation Programs
categories.delivers: a program whose own structure was synthesised and which, when run, produces the simulation
categories.description: Deliver the simulation as code — Python with a physics engine, a Blender script, a scene program — whose structure is itself synthesised from the observations, usually by a language model or a coding agent that runs and revises it.
categories.tagline: code that, when run, is the simulation

categories.title: Learned Simulators
categories.delivers: a trained network whose weights hold the dynamics
categories.description: Learn the simulator itself from real data: particle and graph dynamics models over 3D state, or action-conditioned video world models that predict future observations.
categories.tagline: a network that holds the dynamics

categories.title: Deliver a Runnable Simulation
categories.delivers: a simulation that is executed or compared: a program, a scene file, a 4D world, or equations with parameters
categories.description: The system watches the observations and must hand in something that runs — a program, a scene, a 4D world, or governing equations with parameters — which the benchmark executes or compares with ground truth.
categories.tagline: hand in a program, scene or 4D world

categories.title: Predict or Answer
categories.delivers: answers, labels or outcome predictions, with no generated frames
categories.description: Predict what happens next, or what would happen under a change, from videos of physical scenes; the answer is an outcome, a label or a question answer.

categories.title: Generate the Future
categories.delivers: generated video frames, from video generators or world models
categories.description: Generate the continuation (or the whole clip) and be scored on whether it is physically right: against real held-out footage, physical laws, or human and VLM judges.

categories.title: Does the Simulator Match Reality?
categories.delivers: nothing from a model: the simulator or simulated environment itself is what is tested
categories.description: The object under test is the simulator or simulated environment: do policy success rates, rankings or physical motions in simulation agree with the real world?
categories.tagline: the simulator itself is under test

categories.title: Datasets
categories.description: Recordings, objects and assets that real-to-sim methods learn from or are checked against, without a protocol that scores real-to-sim ability.

categories.title: Surveys
categories.description: Surveys and reviews of real-to-sim and of the fields it draws on.
categories.tagline: reviews of the field and nearby ones

categories.title: Simulations Generated from Text
categories.delivers: tasks, scenes, rewards or simulation code written from a text description
categories.description: Language models write simulation tasks, scenes, rewards or physics code from a text prompt, without looking at the real world.
categories.tagline: simulations written from a text prompt

categories.title: Code World Models
categories.delivers: a program that models a game or simulated environment
categories.description: Programs induced from the state traces of games or simulators to serve as world models for planning.
categories.tagline: programs induced from game or sim traces

categories.title: Learned Simulators without Real Data
categories.delivers: a learned simulator trained on simulated data, or a world generated rather than reproduced
categories.description: Foundational learned simulators trained only on simulator data, and generative world models that invent worlds instead of reproducing a real one.

builders.label: Optimization
builders.description: parameters or structure fitted by differentiable simulation, rendering or search

builders.label: Reconstruction pipeline
builders.description: multi-stage reconstruction, alignment and assembly, sometimes with a person in the loop

builders.label: Feed-forward network
builders.description: a trained network predicts the result in one pass

builders.label: Generative prior
builders.description: a video or 3D generative model supplies motion or parameters

builders.label: LLM / agent
builders.description: a language model or coding agent writes or chooses the result

builders.label: Learned from data
builders.description: the simulator is a network trained on recorded dynamics
